assessments.reasoning: The 2010 DLS account §2.1.2 on PDF page 2, printed page 44, explains that square brackets mark a quotation literal, put the quotation object on the stack, and defer evaluating the enclosed code. Combinators receive quotation objects as arguments, illustrated by the two branches supplied to if.

challenge.method: Compared the conditional example to the surrounding text on quotation objects and to the later parser, accumulator, and parsing-word discussion on PDF pages 7–8.
challenge.results: The conditional consumes two quotation objects and selects the applicable branch. The separate parser examples establish why the delay is about evaluating the code represented by the quotation, while the text still gets parsed and the quotation object constructed.

limitations: This is the described higher-order facility in the 2010 paper. Separate parser effects and later implementation behavior require separate evidence.
